clue.text: Record decisive win finally for white

parts.note: an album is a record, an LP

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of each of the words decisive and win

explanation.surface: A record-breaking album triumph is celebrated by someone dressed in white.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg white is the clear protein part around the yolk, the technical name for it.

clue.text: Rook flies south from farm on old moor

indicators.note: in a down clue, flying south sends the rook letter to the bottom of the word

parts.note: a ranch is a large farm
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A rook flies south from a farm on an old moor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moor' poses as the heath of the scene; it is the verb, to tie up a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To moor a ship is to secure it in place, done by dropping a heavy hook to the seabed.

clue.text: Economical move essentially strategic

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly

indicators.note: essentially takes the letter at the heart of the word strategic

explanation.surface: An economical move is, at heart, strategic.
explanation.definitionFit: A budget airline or hotel is a cheap, low-cost one, so the adjective means economical.

clue.text: See drama unfolding around Queen's Ball

indicators.note: around says the anagram goes about the queen letters
unfolding means the letters of see and drama open out into a new order

explanation.surface: Watch a drama unfold at the Queen's Ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A masked ball is a dance where guests wear disguises, the event named for masks.

clue.text: Pried regularly into US deeds

indicators.note: regularly takes every second letter of the words into US deeds

explanation.surface: Someone pried into American property deeds at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: To poke one's nose into others' affairs is to snoop or meddle in them.

clue.text: Compartment for passenger's drink

definitions.meaning: a small passenger car fixed to the side of a motorcycle
a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice

explanation.surface: A passenger in a private compartment orders a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The motorcycle attachment carries one rider, and the cocktail of the same name is a classic brandy mix.

clue.text: Blame safari company initially over simian attack

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the words safari and company

parts.note: an ape is a simian
to go at someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: A safari firm gets the blame for an ape attack.
explanation.definitionFit: To scapegoat someone is to make them carry the blame for others' faults.

clue.text: Player with chips went up and down

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: peed is slang for went, as in went to the toilet
feeling down means feeling blue, low or sad

explanation.surface: A gambler with chips at the table had a night of ups and downs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player with chips' suggests a poker player, but the chips are silicon ones. 'went up' gives PEED backwards, the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: This IBM chess computer, built from custom chips, beat world champion Garry Kasparov in a 1997 match.

clue.text: Old comic features a bishop's junior colleague?

indicators.note: features means holds inside, so the a sits within the comic's name

parts.note: Charlie Chaplin was the silent-film comedian

explanation.surface: An old comic has a bishop's assistant in his act.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman of lower rank attached to an institution; the question mark flags the chess bishop's theme too.

clue.text: Appear again stripping trees and verges, stopped by 1st of May

indicators.note: stopped by means plugged by, the May letter sits inside
stripping removes the outside letters of trees and verges
1st of takes the opening letter of the word May

explanation.surface: Growth returns after trees and verges are cut back on May Day.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come into view, so doing so once more is to reappear.

clue.text: Established standards in mock exams externally

parts.note: cod as an adjective means mock or sham, as in a cod accent

indicators.note: externally keeps only the outside letters of the word exams

explanation.surface: Mock exams are said to follow the established standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock exams' looks like one phrase, but 'mock' gives COD on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Codes are sets of rules or conventions that fix accepted standards, such as a dress code or building code.

clue.text: Draw of Spooner's patriarchy

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of a two-word phrase are swapped

parts.note: a patriarchy is run by men, giving the first word, male
a patriarchy is a society or nation, giving the second word, state

explanation.surface: A puzzle asks what a drawing of Spooner's patriarchy might be.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of MALE STATE gives the answer, two words read as one.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, a position where the player to move is not in check but has no legal move ends the game as a draw.

clue.text: 'Dunno … he maybe on the end of ward C'

indicators.note: maybe says the letters of the words before it could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: re means on, concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: the end of picks the closing letter of the word ward

explanation.surface: Someone unsure of a location guesses it is at the end of ward C.
explanation.walkthrough: 'C' looks like the name of the ward, but it is the Roman numeral and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: C is the Roman numeral for the number written as 100.

clue.text: See 6
Course of spicy food unfinished on ICU by smoker

indicators.note: unfinished drops the last letter of the dish

parts.note: a curry is spicy food
lum is a Scottish word for a chimney, something that smokes

explanation.surface: A spicy meal is left half-eaten in intensive care beside a smoker.
explanation.definitionFit: A school or college course of study is the full syllabus of subjects.

clue.text: Having issue on drug price reviewed

indicators.note: reviewed says the words on, drug and price are gone over again and arranged differently

explanation.surface: Someone has a problem with how a drug price was reviewed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having issue' looks like having a problem; issue here means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is an old legal word for children, so having issue means producing offspring.

clue.text: Empty remark by priest on allowance

parts.note: latitude is freedom, leeway or allowance

explanation.surface: A priest's remark about allowances rings hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: A trite, overused saying is one that has lost all meaning through repetition.

clue.text: Couldn't decide if San Diego was lousy

indicators.note: lousy means poor, so the letters of San Diego are arranged badly

explanation.surface: Someone couldn't decide whether San Diego was any good.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise over a choice is to struggle painfully with it, unable to settle.

clue.text: Perhaps one with match over in outskirts of Kiev

indicators.note: in puts the middle pieces inside the outer letters
outskirts means the outermost letters of the word Kiev

parts.note: A means one, a single thing
a spar is a boxing match
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A player finishes a match on the edge of Kiev.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' says the answer is an example; the clue around it reads as his description, one who played a famous match.
explanation.definitionFit: This Russian world champion, famously beaten by a computer, is an example of a chess master.

clue.text: Expert on board relative's trailer when train missed

parts.note: a grandma is a relative, with the possessive s kept

indicators.note: missed means the railway word is left out of the word trailer

parts.note: rail stands for train, as in travelling by rail

explanation.surface: An onboard expert examines a relative's trailer after the train was missed.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing RAIL from TRAILER leaves TER.
explanation.definitionFit: The board is a chessboard: this is the top title awarded to a chess player.

clue.text: Floral part of short Persian cover possibly left

indicators.note: short drops the final letter of the floor covering

parts.note: a Persian rug is a kind of carpet, a floor cover

explanation.surface: A flower pattern on a short Persian rug may have been left.
explanation.definitionFit: The carpel is the female reproductive organ of a flower, holding the ovary.

clue.text: Lethargy of Politburo put Stalin in the ascendant

indicators.note: the ascendant means rising, so in a down clue the letters are read upwards
in says the letters sit inside the words Politburo put Stalin, across the word breaks

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The Politburo put Stalin in power while others were sluggish.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft read 'in the ascendant' as one reversal phrase, leaving the hiding unsignalled; 'in' marks the hiding and 'the ascendant' the upward reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed, sluggish state, a deep torpor or listlessness.

clue.text: Certainly not free for cycling

indicators.note: cycling sends the opening letter of the word round to the back

parts.note: open means free, unobstructed

explanation.surface: Someone flatly refuses to let a bike be used for free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cycling' moves the O of OPEN to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal emphatic refusal, a slangy variant of no.

clue.text: Catholic in with another crowd to see magic

indicators.note: in places the Catholic letter within the word with

parts.note: another gives a second C, repeating the Catholic abbreviation
a raft of things is a large number, a crowd

explanation.surface: A Catholic joins another group to watch a magic show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' gives a second C, the one just used for Catholic.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery or the practice of spells is the art of witches, so it means magic.

clue.text: Duke's wife skipping half of dull musical

indicators.note: skipping means passing over, leaving out the letters named

parts.note: a duke's wife is a duchess

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters of dull

explanation.surface: A duchess skips half of a dull musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage show by Tim Rice with ABBA's Benny and Björn, about a Cold War chess championship.

clue.text: Drunk gets pawn in position

indicators.note: gets here means receives, the drunkard's word takes the pawn letter
gets in means the pawn letter goes inside the drunkard's word

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

explanation.surface: A drunk gets a pawned item back in position.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a place or location, so it stands for position.

clue.text: Text English channel pics featuring king in revolution

indicators.note: revolution means turning right round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a rut is a groove or channel

indicators.note: pics featuring a king has the king letter inside pics

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: An English TV channel shows pictures of a king during a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolution' turns round the channel word and the pics with their king together; English is added after, at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Scripture is sacred writing, and a text is a passage of scripture quoted in a sermon.

clue.text: Take in circuit ahead

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track
up means ahead, as in two goals up

explanation.surface: A racer takes in one more circuit while out in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap up something is to accept or absorb it eagerly, like praise or news.

clue.text: Follower of slithy thing from the East in river

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

indicators.note: read from the east, in an across clue, means read from right to left, backwards

parts.note: in Lewis Carroll's Jabberwocky, the slithy toves gyre and gimble

explanation.surface: A disciple hunts a slithy creature from the East in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slithy' is a nonsense word from Lewis Carroll's Jabberwocky, where the toves are slithy. No word marks the insertion into the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A devotee is an ardent fan or disciple, someone who follows a cause or person.

clue.text: Knight crossing main road by city is fairly close

indicators.note: the knight's title crosses, straddles, the road and city letters

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight
MI stands for the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A knight crosses a main road near a city that is fairly close by.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write it MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Things alike but not identical are near each other in nature, resembling one another.
